record.context_brief: Entropy under composition of logistic maps
record.original_question: Let fa(x) = a x(1 − x) and fb(x) = b x(1 − x) be logistic maps on [0, 1], and let h(f) denote topological entropy. Prove or disprove the implication min(h(fa), h(fb)) > 0 ⇒ h(fa ∘ fb) > 0.

evidence.quote: Denote the topological entropy of a continuous map f by h(f).
Open Problem 6.3. In the logistic family, prove or disprove that min{h(fa), h(fb)} > 0 implies that h(fa ◦ fb) > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each real parameter $c\in[0,4]$, let $f_c\colon[0,1]\to[0,1]$ be the logistic map defined by $f_c(x)=c\,x(1-x)$. For a continuous self-map $f$ of a compact metric space, let $h(f)$ denote its topological entropy. Prove or disprove the following statement: for every $a,b\in[0,4]$,
$$\min\{h(f_a),\,h(f_b)\} > 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; h(f_a\circ f_b) > 0.$$
Equivalently, decide whether the "chaos + chaos = order" Parrondo-type paradox can occur in the topological-entropy sense within the logistic family.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether "chaos + chaos = order" can occur in the topological-entropy sense for compositions in the logistic family has been investigated (notably by Cánovas and collaborators on Parrondo's paradox for the logistic family). Numerical computations strongly suggest it cannot happen, while the dual "order + order = chaos" paradox does occur. No proof or counterexample appears to have been published, so the implication is still considered open.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting Parrondo's Paradox for the Logistic Family
status_evidence.snippet: A paradox of type 'order + order = chaos' arises for both physically observable and topological chaos, while a 'chaos + chaos = order' paradox can be only detected for physically observable chaos.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical evidence suggests the topological 'chaos+chaos=order' paradox does not occur for the logistic family, but no proof is given.

status_evidence.title: On the dynamics of the q-deformed logistic map
status_evidence.snippet: Composition of logistic maps and Parrondo's paradox in topological entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Compositions of logistic maps with regard to topological entropy remain an active research topic with open questions.
